_comment: HAND-WRITTEN SAMPLE - this is documentation of the schema, not data.
The runtime loads markers/chapter1.json (no `.sample`), which tools/markers
produces from the cooked .umap cells. Every coordinate below is a real one
taken from the in-world recon dumps in the task workspace, so the file is also
a usable smoke test: rename it to chapter1.json and these seven markers appear
at the places the recon found them.
Stable ids: a shrine uses the game-authored shrine id from BP_RebornFire_C's
CJK-named 'sitting-Buddha point ID' property; everything else uses
<owning level short name>/<cooked actor object name>, because that object name
is what FindAllOf hands back at runtime - it is the join key between this file
Categories: shrine, chest, pickup, boss, elite, enemy, npc, merchant, door,
ladder, lift, fog_gate, hidden, other. An `enemy` entry here is a SPAWN POINT,
not a live enemy: the runtime overwrites its position from the live pawn when
that pawn is streamed in, and enemies are never written to the collection
tracker. That is why the live sweep does not namespace enemy ids - the spawn
point and the live pawn must be one marker, not two.
